reason: Focused court rectification rule listing when the court may direct title-register rectification and how applications are made.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Court orders directing rectification of the title register
proposedGroups.reason: The subsections list entitlement, aggrieved-entry, fraud, wrongful act, and mistake grounds and point applications to section 79.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Explain when the court may order rectification of the title register.

reason: Rule protecting a registered owner in possession from detrimental rectification except in specified knowledge, void disposition, or injustice cases.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Rectification affecting a registered owner in possession

evidenceText: shall not be rectified so as to affect detrimentally the title of the registered owner who is in possession
unless

proposedGroups.reason: The text states the protective rule and exceptions for knowledge, causing or contributing, void dispositions, or unjust refusal to rectify.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify when rectification may detrimentally affect a registered owner in possession.

reason: Focused notation rule for rectification and when the rectification is deemed effective.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Notation and timing of title-register rectification
proposedGroups.reason: The subsections require notation without erasing erroneous entries and deem rectification effective from the original error or omission time.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Explain how rectification is noted and when it is deemed to have taken effect.

reason: Indemnification on rectification has separate entitlement and exception rules and a special forged-disposition damage rule.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Indemnity for rectification, errors, omissions, or lost documents
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 73(1) states when damaged persons are entitled to indemnity and lists exceptions for fraud, negligence, available recovery actions, notice, trust breach, and necessary delay.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify when a person is entitled to indemnity and the main exceptions.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Forged disposition deemed damage on rectification
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 73(2) deems a good-faith value owner under a forged disposition to have suffered damage when the title register is rectified.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: State how a forged disposition affects deemed damage for indemnity.

reason: Focused indemnity-award process through the Registrar General or court.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Award of indemnity by Registrar General or court
proposedGroups.reason: The subsections allow Registrar General determination and award with approvals and consent, and court application if an award is not made.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Explain how a claimant may obtain an indemnity award.

reason: Single payment rule requiring assignment of rights before indemnity payment.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Payment of indemnity and assignment of rights

evidenceText: shall be paid forthwith
executing in favour of the Registrar General an assignment of any rights

proposedGroups.reason: The text connects indemnity payment to assignment of enforceable rights to the Registrar General.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: State what must be assigned before an indemnity is paid.

reason: Registrar General recovery power after indemnity is paid.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Recovery of indemnity payments from third parties

evidenceText: may take proceedings to recover the amount so paid
caused or substantially contributed to the damage by his fraud or negligence

proposedGroups.reason: The section authorizes recovery from fraud or negligence contributors and enforcement of rights the indemnified person could enforce.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Explain when the Registrar General may recover an indemnity payment from third parties.

reason: Focused agreement power for Service New Brunswick about liability arising from indemnity recovery.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Agreements respecting liability for indemnity payments

evidenceText: enter into agreements with the Law Society of New Brunswick
with respect to liability under that section

proposedGroups.reason: The text permits agreements with the Law Society, its members, or others about liability under section 76.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: State with whom Service New Brunswick may make liability agreements for indemnity recovery.

reason: The target contains only a repeal note.
Valuation rule for indemnity where damage involves loss of an estate, interest, or encumbrance, including good-faith improvements.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Time of valuation for indemnity
proposedGroups.reason: The subsections cap indemnity by fair market value at the relevant error or rectification time and include good-faith later improvements.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Explain how indemnity value is timed and when improvements are included.

reason: Single two-year commencement rule for indemnity applications.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Two-year limitation period for indemnity applications

evidenceText: shall be commenced within and not later than two years
from the date that the applicant knew of the event

proposedGroups.reason: The section requires indemnity applications to start within two years of knowledge of the damage-causing event.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: State the limitation period for indemnity applications.

reason: Court application section separates decision reasons and applications, notice and title-register effects, and timing or hearing powers.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Reasons and applications to court for decisions or rectification
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections define decision, allow written reasons requests, and authorize court applications for rectification or dissatisfaction with a decision.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Explain who may seek reasons or apply to court about rectification or a land titles decision.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Notice of proposed court application and effect on dealings
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections require notice to the Registrar General, registrar notation, dealings subject to notice, and protection for prior good-faith value dispositions.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Describe the notice procedure before a court application and its effect on dealings with land.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Time limit, evidence, and court orders on applications
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections set the thirty-day application limit, allow relevant evidence, and authorize orders and costs subject to section 71.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: State the time limit, evidence rule, and order power for land titles court applications.

reason: Fees section separates registration and assurance fees, value evidence, and accounting or indemnity payment funds.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Registration, electronic payment, and assurance fees
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections require prescribed fees before registrar action, electronic payment for electronic instruments, assurance fees, and Crown-transfer assurance fee exemptions.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify fee, electronic payment, assurance fee, and Crown-transfer exemption rules.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Affidavit or declaration of value for transfers
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections require value affidavits or electronic declarations, apply related statutes, and allow evaluator certificates if value is not satisfactory.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Explain how land value is established before a transfer is registered.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Registrar accounts and funds for indemnity payments
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections govern registrar accounts, payment of indemnity from a dedicated account or fund, and Consolidated Fund payment if needed.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Describe how registrar money and indemnity payment funds are handled.

reason: Single affidavit requirement for marital status when registered owners execute listed instruments.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Affidavit of marital status for registered owner instruments

evidenceText: registered owner who executes a transfer, mortgage, lease or easement
shall make an affidavit of marital status

proposedGroups.reason: The section states the prescribed-form marital status affidavit requirement and listed instruments.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: State when a registered owner must make an affidavit of marital status.

reason: Focused public request rule for registered information, fees, and registrar liability limits.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Requests for registered land information
proposedGroups.reason: The subsections require information access on request, prescribed fee payment, and limit registrar liability unless information is certified.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Explain how registered information is requested and when registrar liability can arise.

reason: The target is a broad regulation-making provision listing land titles subjects such as fees, officer duties, forms, electronic instruments, service, offices, parcel standards, records, and related administration.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Land Titles Act regulation-making powers

evidenceText: may make regulations
authorizing and prescribing fees
prescribing duties and powers of the Registrar General or a registrar
designating instruments that are to be submitted in electronic format
prescribing standards for descriptions of parcels of land

proposedGroups.reason: The section is a single list of matters the Lieutenant-Governor in Council may regulate for land titles administration.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the main subjects that may be governed by Land Titles Act regulations.

reason: Transitional deeming rule translating Registry Act and registry-office references into Land Titles Act equivalents for registered land.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Transitional references from Registry Act system to land titles system

evidenceText: reference is made
such reference shall be deemed to be to this Act
where the land in respect of which the reference applies is registered land

proposedGroups.reason: The provision deems references to Registry Act provisions, offices, registrars of deeds, deeds, registration, and filing to mean land titles equivalents for registered land.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Explain how transitional references are read for registered land under the Land Titles Act.

reason: The target only repeals the former 1914 Land Titles Act and does not provide an ongoing study rule.
